title: Type names: Spark's (`tinyint` … `bigint`, `float`, `double`, `decimal(p,s)`, `timestamp_ntz`)
verdict: `typeof` gives Spark's names; `TIMESTAMP` is `timestamp` (LTZ) or `timestamp_ntz` by setting
description: `typeof` names `tinyint`, `smallint`, `int`, `bigint`, `float`, `double`, `decimal(p,s)`, `string`, `binary`, `boolean`, `date`, `timestamp` (with a local time zone), `timestamp_ntz`, `interval day`, `interval month`, `array<…>`, `map<…>`, `variant`, `void` for NULL. Aliases parse: `BYTE`, `SHORT`, `INTEGER`, `LONG`, `REAL`, `DEC` (`decimal(10,0)`), `NUMERIC`. `VARCHAR(n)` and `CHAR(n)` in a cast are plain `string` and keep every character (`CAST('abcd' AS VARCHAR(3))` is `abcd`). `TIMESTAMP` means `timestamp_ntz` under `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.
reference: `typeof` folds to DuckDB's names whichever engine runs the plan (duckdb-typeof-names). The SQL writer names Spark's types itself (`sverify.sql.spark`).

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_spark` runs each query four times on one local session: with `spark.sql.ansi.enabled` true and false, on the folded path (the optimizer evaluates a query over `VALUES` on the driver) and on the codegen path (`ConvertToLocalRelation` and `ConstantFolding` excluded, so the query runs as a job with whole-stage code generation). probes.json keeps one result per ANSI setting where the two paths agree. Spark 4.3.0 (pyspark 4.3.0), Java 21.0.12, Linux x86_64, `local[2]`, session time zone UTC, `spark.sql.timestampType=TIMESTAMP_NTZ`.
